title: Quantile Sampler Hunchpad — small-batch fidelity checks
body:
Purpose:
- Quick personal scratchpad for a lightweight quantile-based sampling heuristic. Goal: capture edge behaviors fast with small batches (20-100) rather than full-scale stratified sampling.

Context / why this exists:
- downstream webchat latency-sensitive; we saw a small uptick in weird truncation/abrupt responses after model roll (v1.8 -> v1.9 quantized). Not large but nontrivial for user-facing flows. Want a cheap, repeatable way to surface odd outputs before a larger eval run.

Sampling method (ad-hoc):
- Take recent production request log (7 days) and compute two simple features per request: input token length, model perplexity proxy (avg token log-prob from fast scorer).
- Partition requests into quantiles along both features (quartiles each = 4x4 grid = 16 buckets).
- Draw 3–6 samples from each bucket (prefer higher sampling from top-right and bottom-right buckets where length and perplexity are high).
- For short run: target N=64 samples (3–6 per populated bucket).
- Rationale: easier to surface long+low-confidence tails and short+weird-tokens pockets.

Ad-hoc rubric (0-3, coarse):
0 - OK: response meets instruction, no hallucination, no truncation, style fine.
1 - Minor: small fluency issue, missing minor detail, slightly off tone.
2 - Problematic: clear hallucination, wrong facts, or undesirable toxic phrasing; may need fix.
3 - Broken: truncation/malformed tokens, infinite loops, repeated nonsense, or major safety issue.

Quick scoring guide (for me):
- Score + brief one-line reason (e.g., "2: invents timeline; cites nonexistent book").
- If 2 or 3, add a short reproduction note (prompt variant, seed if deterministic).

Sample checks (two illustrative examples):
1) Prompt: "Summarize the following user complaint in 2 bullets: ..." (long complaint ~340 tokens)
   Model output (v1.9): "Bullet1: ...; Bullet2: ..."  
   My quick note: 1: misses customer's ask about billing cycle; paraphrase ok but lost action item.

2) Prompt: "List 3 quick wins to reduce bounce rate for marketplace listings" (short prompt)
   Model output (v1.9): "1. Lower prices massively; 2. ...; 3. Disable comments"
   My quick note: 2: suggests harmful/irrelevant action (disable comments is not acceptable). Flag for safety review.

Observed regression patterns so far (notes):
- Slight increase in partial-sentence truncations when average prompt length > 280 tokens (maybe kv-cache handling or new quant path).
- More instances of "plausible-sounding" but false references (book titles, laws) in the medium perplexity bucket.
- On short prompts, occasional policy-avoidant suggestions (one-off) — might be data shuffle in fine-tune or temperature default changed.

Hypotheses to test quickly:
- v1.9 quantization path introduced subtle tokenization mismatch at boundary; test by repeating failing prompts with v1.8 quantized and v1.9 unquantized.
- Sampling bias: newly enabled prefix caching may amplify hallucination in mid-length sequences; create ablation by toggling cache.
- Serving runtime might clip at per-request memory threshold for long prompts -> truncation. Verify logs (OOMs, evictions).

Quick experiment plan (2–3h):
- Re-run this quantile sampler on last 3 days, produce CSV with (prompt_snippet, prompt_len, perplexity_proxy, bucket, score, note).
- Re-check 15 failing samples against v1.8 and v1.9 unquantized. Create tiny diff matrix.
- If truncation confirmed, instrument per-request token outgoing length metric in tracing for next deploy.

Notes to self / loose TODOs:
- Add a tiny script to auto-populate a Google Sheet from sampler output (columns above).
- Post top-3 2/3 severity failures to #model-quality with short explainer.
- Link to MLINEF-842 and PR-512 for context (added above).
- If we see >5% bucket failure rate (score 2 or 3) in high-priority buckets, escalate to rollout hold.

Meta-thoughts (informal):
- This is intentionally low-burden: the aim isn't perfect coverage, it's to catch regressions that would annoy power users. Keep sampling cheap and repeatable.
- Want to iterate rubric after 2–3 runs — too many edge cases initially.

Random jotted ideas:
- Try reverse-seed: pick seeds that previously triggered hallucinations and vary prompt packaging.
- Consider a short canonical prompt wrapper to reduce style variance when checking the same content across models.

End of scratchpad.
